title: Decision authorities
intro: Decision authorities are the places in the app that hand a decision to a decision provider: a model that answers typed questions (yes/no, pick one, rate) in a fraction of a second. Each authority can stay off, run in shadow (asked in the background and measured next to the existing logic, changing nothing) or be switched on, and each can use its own provider with a fallback and a challenger.
privacy: What is judged (a shell command, a coordinator message, a flow output, a transcript excerpt) is sent to the decision model after obvious secrets are masked. A model on your own machine keeps it local.
enabledHint: Master switch. While off nothing is sent anywhere and every authority behaves as before.
defaultModelHint: Answers for every authority that names no provider of its own.

account.title: Provider account
account.text: Add an OpenRouter account under provider instances and enter its API key. Not needed if you use a local model (LM Studio, Ollama, OpenJev) or give a decision provider its own key.

provider.title: Decision provider
provider.text: Add one with “+ New decision provider” (the “Jev · OpenRouter” template borrows the account above), then press Test on its card.

enable.title: Decision authorities
enable.text: On the Decision authorities screen turn on “Use the decision layer”; run authorities in Shadow first and switch them On once the agreement is high.

providers.title: Decision providers
providers.hint: Models that answer typed questions instead of chatting: Jev (OpenRouter, TypeSafe), OpenJev or any local model (Ollama, LM Studio). They never appear in an agent's model picker.
providers.openAuthorities: Choose where they are used under Decision authorities →
providers.empty: No decision provider yet. Add one with the button above.
providers.confirmDelete: Are you sure you want to delete the decision provider "{{label}}"?
providers.deletedUsed: Decision provider deleted. These now use the default provider: {{list}}
providers.testOk: Answered in {{ms}} ms · {{cost}} · needs approval: {{probability}} · risk level {{level}}

form.label: Label
form.labelPlaceholder: Label (e.g. OpenJev on the GPU box)
form.modelCustomPlaceholder: The model id as the server lists it
form.credentialsProviderHint: Uses the key and endpoint of that provider; no key is entered twice.
form.providerMissing: No usable provider account for this kind. Add one above, or use an own endpoint and key.
form.apiKeyRequired: This kind needs an API key.
form.timeoutHint: A timed-out call is retried once; then the authority falls back.
form.contextHint: Empty = the kind's {{tokens}}. Lower it for a local server started with a small context.
form.localFree: Runs on this machine or network: no token cost.
form.uncalibrated: Reads an ordinary model's token probabilities: useful, but not calibrated like Jev.

openrouter.label: OpenRouter Decisions
openrouter.description: OpenRouter's Decisions API (alpha). Serves TypeSafe's Jev: yes/no, pick-one and score answers with calibrated probabilities in well under a second.

systemone.label: System One API (TypeSafe · OpenJev)
systemone.description: TypeSafe's native decision API and every server that speaks it: TypeSafe itself, OpenRouter's System One endpoint, and open OpenJev servers running a decision model on your own hardware.

llm-logprobs.label: Any LLM (token probabilities)
llm-logprobs.description: Turns an ordinary chat model into a decision model: each question is asked as a one-letter multiple choice and the answer's probabilities are read from the model's token probabilities. Works with Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM and any OpenAI-compatible server that returns logprobs.

suffix.label: Question suffix
suffix.help: Appended to every question. Hybrid reasoning models must answer at once: /no_think for Qwen3.

extraBody.label: Extra request fields (JSON)
extraBody.help: Merged into every request body, e.g. to switch reasoning off on vLLM or llama.cpp.

topLogprobs.label: Top logprobs
topLogprobs.help: Alternatives read per token (1-20). Options outside them count as zero.

maxTokens.label: Max answer tokens
maxTokens.help: Tokens the model may spend before its label (an empty <think></think> block, a leading space).

parallel.label: Parallel questions
parallel.help: Questions asked at once. Lower it if the server runs one request at a time.

jev-openrouter.label: Jev · OpenRouter
jev-openrouter.description: TypeSafe Jev through the key of an OpenRouter provider you already have.

jev-typesafe.label: Jev · TypeSafe
jev-typesafe.description: TypeSafe's own API with a TypeSafe API key.

jev-openrouter-systemone.label: Jev · OpenRouter (System One)
jev-openrouter-systemone.description: OpenRouter's System One endpoint through the key of an OpenRouter provider you already have.

openjev-local.label: OpenJev · this machine
openjev-local.description: An OpenJev server on this computer (docker compose up, default port 8080). Free and private; needs a GPU.

ollama-local.label: Ollama · this machine
ollama-local.description: A model served by Ollama on this computer (port 11434).

lmstudio-local.label: LM Studio · this machine
lmstudio-local.description: The model loaded in LM Studio's local server (port 1234).

authorities.title: Decision authorities
authorities.hint: Every place in the app that can hand a decision to a decision provider. Start in shadow, watch the agreement, switch on when you trust it. A fallback answers when the provider cannot; a challenger is asked the same question in the background, so a new provider can be measured before it takes over.
authorities.failClosedHint: When no model can answer it refuses (the gate stays shut) instead of falling back.

stall-judge.label: Coordinator stall judge
stall-judge.description: Does the coordinator's last message claim it opened workers it never opened? Replaces a Haiku call per idle coordinator turn.
stall-judge.threshold: Minimum probability of "stalled" before the coordinator is nudged.

tool-risk.label: Shell command risk check
tool-risk.description: A second look at shell commands that would run without asking (auto mode or an "always allow" rule such as git *). When on, a risky command becomes an approval prompt; an unattended run is never blocked.
tool-risk.threshold: Minimum probability that the command needs approval before you are asked.

flow-judge.label: Flow judge nodes
flow-judge.description: Branch and loop nodes in the "judge" match mode let the model pick the arm or decide the loop's exit condition instead of matching text.
flow-judge.threshold: Minimum probability for an arm to be taken (otherwise the default arm) or for the exit condition to count as met.

phase-gate.label: Rota judge gates
phase-gate.description: Phase gates of kind "judge" ask whether the phase's exit condition holds, judged against the root session's recent transcript. If no model can answer, the gate stays shut.
phase-gate.threshold: Minimum probability that the exit condition holds before the gate opens.

modeHint.shadow: Asked in the background and recorded next to the current decision; changes nothing.
modeHint.on: Its answer is used; on an error the previous logic takes over.

stats.title: Last {{days}} days
stats.agreementHint: Share of shadow comparisons in which the model reached the same decision as the existing logic.
stats.readyToSwitch: High agreement: ready to switch on.
stats.keepShadow: Low agreement: keep it in shadow.
stats.challengerReady: The challenger agrees often enough to take over.
stats.challengerKeep: The challenger disagrees too often to take over.
